reference.title: PDF rendering and limits
reference.shortdesc: How PDFs are printed, what the renderer needs, and what it cannot do yet.

section.title: The renderer
section.p: A headless Chromium, driven by playwright-core, prints the publication's self-contained HTML. One browser is launched on the first request and reused.

ul.li: Each document gets a fresh browser context with JavaScript disabled, and every network request is refused. Authored content therefore cannot make the server fetch a URL.
At most two documents print at once; others wait. Each has 60 seconds to load and print.
Pages are A4 with 20 mm top, 18 mm side and bottom margins.
The server image includes Debian's Chromium and sets OPEND_CHROMIUM_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium.
Outside Docker, install a browser with pnpm exec playwright-core install chromium in the OpenD checkout, or point OPEND_CHROMIUM_PATH at one.
Chromium's own sandbox is off by default, because unprivileged containers usually cannot create the namespaces it needs. OPEND_CHROMIUM_SANDBOX=1 turns it on where the runtime allows it.
The contents list has links but no page numbers: Chromium does not support target-counter(). Use the PDF outline for page-accurate navigation.
The header and footer also appear on the cover.
External images (https: URLs) are not loaded, because the renderer refuses network requests. Keep images in the project.
url() references in the theme are not resolved.
The first request for a new release and entitlement set takes a moment, about a second for a small manual. Later requests are served from the cache.
